answer: Each agent earns reputation only after a counterparty locks a refundable stake and completes a task; disputes can slash the stake, while successful trades slowly raise the agent’s limit. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many independent stakes and keep them exposed through repeated trades, rather than minting cheap identities. A gale of fabricated accounts cannot share one deposit, and a raven or vine of colluding agents still risks losing capital when they default or are challenged.
